items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: I remember going down into the old district where he was playing in Storyville to hire him to go for those dances.

ctx.x: Are they sleeping quarters now? I really don't know. I doubt they're sleeping quarters now, unless maybe for the offices.

Well, it could be that, but they had always the finest jazz bands in the city available at that time. Joe Oliver was the most popular band of all, and I remember going down into the old district where he was playing in Storyville to hire him to go for those dances. It was from 8 to 12, and that was it, unless they took up a... Pass the hat and got enough money to keep them to one o'clock, and that was the limit.

Well, do you think you could, as closely as possible, trace the... Use of jazz bands for entertainment from then down to now, and also the interest in it as a form of music, and the attitude of white New Orleans...

items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: And I don't know who else has told you this, but we never knew him as Joe Oliver. We called him Monocle.

ctx.x: Oh, little slits in the side?

Yeah. Oh, like just up and down, straight across. They could just open up like that. I also remember him wearing a red undershirt and suspenders. And he'd cock that derby hat over that bad eye. And I don't know who else has told you this, but we never knew him as Joe Oliver. We called him Monocle. When he blew that bad eye, which was a white eye, he sustained a traumatic cataract in a fight, and that eye was perfectly white.
